svg.title: Fabric Capacity Sizing: Scale Up, Autoscale Spark, or Split Workloads?
svg.desc: A decision infographic for Fabric capacity sizing: evaluate root cause of CU contention, then choose between scaling up the F-SKU ladder, enabling Autoscale Billing for Spark, or splitting workloads across capacities for throttling isolation.
svg.text: Fabric Capacity Sizing — Scale-Up vs Autoscale vs Split
Decision framework for Capacity Unit (CU) exhaustion, bursty workloads, and SLA isolation

g.title: What's driving capacity contention? — Root question: identify which workload shape is causing throttling before picking a remedy.
g.text: A capacity is showing sustained CU pressure / throttling
What is the actual workload shape driving contention?

g.title: Evaluate a SKU increase — For predictable but genuinely CU-constrained load, move up the doubling F-SKU ladder.
g.text: LANE A · SCALE UP THE SKU
When to Use:
• Sustained future-usage across ALL workloads
• Consistent Stage 1/2 throttling thresholds
• Predictable aggregate growth across teams
SKU = CU Count: Each step doubles compute capacity
F-SKU Doubling Ladder & Benefits
Dev/Test & Departmental
Free-viewer license threshold
Enterprise Scale Data Mesh
Downstream Multiplier Effects:
• Spark vCore Ceiling: CU × 2 × 3 burst cap
F64 (384 vCores) ➔ F128 (768 vCores)
• Direct Lake RAM Limit: Memory cap rises
Prevents cold paging & DirectQuery fallbacks
• Smoothing Buffer: Larger headroom absorbing
transient 24h background ETL spikes
✓ Instant SKU scaling via Azure Portal with zero downtime

g.title: Enable Autoscale Billing for Spark — Move bursty, unpredictable Spark usage to pay-as-you-go, outside the shared smoothed CU pool.
g.text: LANE B · AUTOSCALE SPARK
When to Use:
• Spark notebooks / ad-hoc jobs spike unpredictably
• Capacity is otherwise right-sized for reports
• Want pay-as-you-go isolation for burst compute
Isolates Spark from shared smoothed CU consumption pool
Autoscale Billing Mechanics
• Spark usage switches to Azure PAYG billing
• Stops drawing from capacity's fixed CU quota
• Spark jobs spin up dynamic nodes on-demand
• Power BI reports / Warehouse remain 100% protected
Protects capacity SLA without permanent SKU cost hike

g.aria-label: Trap: Autoscale Spark drops bursting and smoothing
g.title: Trap: Autoscale Spark drops bursting and smoothing — When enabled, Spark usage switches to pay-as-you-go and stops drawing from the smoothed CU pool.
g.text: CRITICAL TRAP
Bypasses Bursting & Smoothing
• Autoscale Billing Spark does NOT smooth over 24h.
• Billed immediately per second of PAYG execution.
• Can lead to unexpected Azure invoice charges
if run on runaway unoptimized queries.
Remedy: Set max vCore autoscale limits on Spark pool.
Tracked in capacity governance policies.

g.title: Split across separate capacities — When one workload's throttling threatens another's SLA, separate them since throttling is enforced per capacity.
g.text: LANE C · SPLIT CAPACITIES
When to Use:
• ETL throttling risks breaking Executive BI dashboards
• Multi-department chargeback & cost governance
• Production SLAs require 100% hard isolation
Fabric throttling is strictly PER-CAPACITY, never per-tenant
Workload Split Architecture
Capacity 1: BI (F64)
Protected SLA Uptime
Capacity 2: ETL (F32)
Heavy Batch & Spark

g.aria-label: Why splitting works: per-capacity throttling boundary
g.title: Why splitting works: per-capacity throttling boundary — Throttling is enforced per capacity, not per tenant, so an isolated capacity's saturation never touches a different capacity's budget.
g.text: PER-CAPACITY THROTTLING ISOLATION
OneLake Shortcuts & Blast Radius:
• Zero Data Duplication: Both capacities query same
OneLake tables via Shortcuts with zero cross-tenant lag
• Hard Isolation: Heavy batch overages on Cap 2
NEVER cause interactive delays on Cap 1
✓ Independent scaling, pause/resume, and cost allocation
Sourced from Fabric Entra Tenancy & Capacity Isolation.

g.title: Sizing checklist: three ceilings — Check the Spark vCore ceiling, Direct Lake memory ceiling, and F64 licensing threshold before finalizing a SKU.
g.text: FINAL SIZING CHECKLIST · 3 HARD ARCHITECTURAL CEILINGS
Spark vCore Burst Limit
Max vCores = CU × 2 × 3 (e.g. F64 = 384 vCores, F128 = 768 vCores).
Jobs requiring more cores must use autoscale pool or larger SKU.
Direct Lake Memory Cap
Resident model columns cannot exceed capacity SKU RAM quota.
Breaching cap causes cold-read DirectQuery fallbacks.
F64 Free-Viewer Threshold
Broad viewing with free Fabric licenses requires F64 or larger.
SKUs < F64 require Pro/PPU licenses for every report viewer.
Fabric Atlas — Original Decision Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Capacity Architecture.
